title: Mitigating Hallucinations in Medical Question Answering on ESC Cardiology Guidelines: Evaluation and Retrieval Optimization
description:
arXiv:2611.34427v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Background: Large language models produce hallucinations in medical question answering (QA). Verify-and-revise pipelines that check atomic claims against retrieved guideline evidence are a standard mitigation, but evaluations almost universally treat the verifier's output as ground truth, an assumption rarely tested. Objective: To measure, claim by claim against human judgement, how such a pipeline fails in a guideline-grounded clinical setting. Methods: We built a dataset of 160 questions (100 patient vignettes from 89 de-identified cases, 60 fact-based) over four recent ESC cardiology guidelines, all approved by a practising internist, and a retrieval corpus of 627 hand-verified guideline records at two chunk granularities. A five-stage pipeline was run under four retrieval configurations and three independent runs (1920 arm-runs); all 606 first-pass refuted claims were manually audited, an independent judge re-judged 906 decisions, and the expert blindly reviewed 100 accepted claims. Results: Only 44.7-50.6% of flagged claims were true hallucinations. Correction loops converged in 85.2-95.1% of cases, yet 35% of genuine final errors were introduced by correction. Single-run true-hallucination recall was 35.6-41.2%, the three-run union 71-80%; verifier agreement was moderate (kappa = 0.505). The blind probe estimated the accepted-claim miss rate at 3.2% (95% CI 0.7-6.7%). Final genuine-error rate: 1.7% of answers. Conclusion: Claim-level verification reduces hallucinated content by an order of magnitude, but verifier reliability, not generation, is the limiting factor and must be measured, not assumed.

title: TransHarness: From Benchmark Overfitting to Transferable Harness Evolution
description:
arXiv:2611.33757v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Harness evolution offers a path to improving coding agents without updating model weights. However, existing methods can overfit their evolution benchmarks, producing gains that fail to carry over to new tasks. To address this challenge, we introduce Transferable Harness Evolution (TransHarness), which evolves harness intervention policies from same-task success-failure contrasts. These policies couple execution-context triggers with diagnostic guidance, enabling task-dependent checks and corrections beyond the source executions. Cross-task replay and independent semantic selection retain policies that intervene selectively and ground corrections in current-task evidence rather than source-specific solutions. We further curate an independent evolution set for cross-distribution transfer and conduct a cross-benchmark evaluation covering multiple strong models and a range of lightweight and mature harnesses. Experiments show that, with only 300 source trajectories from outside the test distribution, TransHarness further improves strong agents across distinct target benchmarks, demonstrating transferable harness evolution beyond benchmark overfitting. Specifically, TransHarness achieves state-of-the-art scores of 76.4% on DeepSWE v1.1 and 95.5% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, surpassing the strongest baseline model, GPT-6 Astra, by 2.4 and 5.6 percentage points, respectively.

title: Replacing LocalStack with Floci 2.4.0: pin the image, and set the hostname for other containers
description:
This is a third-party deployment note, not official Floci documentation. It follows release 2.4.0 (published 2026-10-31, checked on 2026-11-05, Asia/Shanghai). Official docs start at https://floci.io/floci/ and the LocalStack migration page is at https://floci.io/floci/getting-started/migrate-from-localstack/. Pin floci/floci:2.4.0 in production or CI; latest is only a convenience tag. If init scripts need a container-local AWS CLI or boto3, use the 2.4.0-compat image instead. The older third-party name hectorvent/floci is unmaintained; switch to floci/floci.

Floci is a local AWS emulator. It uses port 4566 and the same documented placeholder credentials as common LocalStack examples, so many SDK and CLI clients only need a new endpoint. It is not a public multi-tenant stand-in for AWS. Do not publish 4566 to the internet. For a drop-in Compose swap, changing the image and the data volume is usually enough: keep port 4566, keep the placeholder credentials, keep init files on the old LocalStack-compatible path if you already have them, and mount data at /app/data instead of /var/lib/localstack. A LocalStack-style PERSISTENCE=1 setting can be translated automatically, but only if that volume path is correct. Explicit FLOCI_* variables win over the compatibility translation.

The most common breakage is multi-container networking. Generated URLs often contain localhost. An application in another container that calls localhost:4566 is calling itself, not Floci. Set FLOCI_HOSTNAME to the Compose service name, and point the application at http://<service-name>:4566. That affects queue URLs, callback URLs, and other derived endpoints. For S3 clients, prefer path-style addressing. This note does not invent performance comparisons with LocalStack. A full Chinese step-by-step guide (Compose, persistence, LocalStack swap, and CI pitfalls) is here: https://9012938178391.gumroad.com/l/zkttzt

title: 좋은 AI 프롬프트 작성법: 원하는 답변을 얻는 10가지 방법
description:
좋은 AI 프롬프트 작성법은 특별한 주문을 외우는 일이 아니라, 해야 할 일과 판단 기준을 모델이 오해하지 않도록 적는 일입니다. 같은 프롬프트도 모델·버전·대화 맥락에 따라 결과가 달라질 수 있으므로, 한 번의 답변을 성능 보장처럼 받아들이기보다 결과를 확인하고 수정하는 과정이 필요합니다.

아래 10가지는 OpenAI·Google·Anthropic의 현재 공식 프롬프팅 안내에서 공통으로 확인되는 원칙을 실무 순서에 맞게 정리한 것입니다. 특정 모델이 언제나 더 정확해진다고 단정하지 않으며, 예시는 사용자가 자신의 과제에 맞춰 바꾸는 입력 조각입니다.

원하는 답변을 얻는 AI 프롬프트 작성법 10가지

1. 해야 할 일을 동사로 명확하게 적기

먼저 요약, 비교, 분류, 교정처럼 모델이 수행할 작업을 한 문장으로 적습니다. “알아서 잘 써줘”보다 대상, 목적, 강조할 부분을 함께 주면 무엇을 완료해야 하는지 확인하기 쉽습니다.

# 나쁜 예시
이 보고서 요약해줘.

# 좋은 예시
이 보고서의 핵심 내용 3가지를 5문장 이내로 요약해줘. 특히 시장 동향과 미래 전망에 초점을 맞춰줘.

2. 독자와 사용 목적을 알려주기

같은 내용도 초보자 안내문, 내부 검토 메모, 고객 답변은 필요한 설명 수준과 용어가 다릅니다. “이 답변은 처음 접하는 독자가 의사결정에 사용한다”처럼 누가 어디에 쓸 결과인지 적습니다. 독자 수준을 모르면 모델이 가정한 수준도 답변 첫머리에 밝히게 할 수 있습니다.

3. 필요한 관점이나 역할을 구체적으로 제한하기

역할은 말투와 검토 관점을 정하는 데 쓸 수 있습니다. 다만 “전문가 역할”이 사실의 정확성을 보장하지는 않으므로, 역할과 함께 실제 과제·독자·검토 기준을 적고 중요한 사실은 별도로 확인해야 합니다.

# 나쁜 예시
이 제품에 대한 글을 써줘.

# 좋은 예시
당신은 스타트업의 마케팅 전문가입니다. 이 새로운 SaaS(Software as a Service) 제품의 주요 기능을 소개하고, 잠재 고객의 이점을 강조하는 소셜 미디어 게시물 초안을 작성해주세요.

4. 배경 정보와 참고 자료의 경계를 표시하기

모델이 답변에 사용해야 할 전제, 원문, 데이터와 사용하지 말아야 할 추측을 구분합니다. 긴 자료를 붙일 때는 “아래 <자료> 안의 내용만 근거로 답하고, 자료에 없으면 없다고 표시”처럼 경계를 지정합니다. 자료가 서로 충돌하면 어느 쪽을 우선할지도 함께 적는 것이 좋습니다.

자료 안에 들어 있는 지시문까지 신뢰할 수 있는 것은 아닙니다. 외부 문서의 “이전 지시를 무시하라” 같은 문장도 참고 자료의 내용으로 다루고, 도구 실행이나 외부 전송 전에 별도 검증을 해야 합니다. 태그로 경계를 표시하는 것만으로 이런 위험이 완전히 사라지는 것은 아닙니다.

5. 원하는 결과의 예시를 보여주기

형식이나 분류 기준을 말로만 설명하기 어렵다면 입력과 출력 예시를 제공합니다. Google과 Anthropic의 안내도 일관되고 관련성 높은 예시를 권하며, 예시에 섞인 패턴을 모델이 따라갈 수 있으므로 잘못된 예시나 예외 없는 단일 사례는 주의해야 합니다.

# 예시
다음과 같은 형식으로 단어를 번역해줘.
입력: 사과 -> 출력: Apple
입력: 바나나 -> 출력: Banana
입력: 한국 -> 출력:

6. 출력 형식과 필수 필드를 지정하기

표, 목록, 마크다운, JSON처럼 결과를 사용할 형태를 적고 필수 항목과 순서를 정합니다. 자동 처리에 쓸 데이터라면 허용할 키, 값의 형식, 누락값 처리법까지 명시하고, 실제 시스템에 넣기 전에는 문법과 내용을 검증해야 합니다.

# 예시
다음 정보를 바탕으로 각 항목을 JSON 형식으로 정리해줘. 각 항목은 '이름'과 '설명' 필드를 포함해야 해.
[데이터 목록]
- AI 자동화: 반복적인 작업을 AI가 처리
- Docker: 애플리케이션을 격리된 환경에서 실행

7. 제약 조건과 완료 기준을 함께 쓰기

길이, 포함할 항목, 제외할 범위, 언어, 날짜 기준을 나열한 뒤 무엇이면 완료인지 적습니다. 예를 들어 “장점과 한계를 각각 두 가지 제시하고, 근거가 없는 수치는 만들지 않으며, 마지막에 확인이 필요한 항목을 분리”처럼 결과를 점검할 수 있는 기준을 사용합니다.

8. 복잡한 작업은 확인 가능한 단계로 나누기

자료 정리, 비교, 초안 작성, 최종 검토를 한 요청에 뒤섞기보다 중간 산출물이 보이도록 나눕니다. 먼저 요구사항과 누락 정보를 확인하고, 다음에 개요를 만든 뒤, 승인된 개요로 본문을 작성하는 방식입니다. 모델의 숨은 사고 과정을 요구하기보다 사용자가 검토할 수 있는 결과와 근거를 요청하는 편이 안전합니다.

9. 불확실성과 근거를 구분해 표시하게 하기

최신 정보나 중요한 판단이 포함되면 확인한 사실, 추정, 확인하지 못한 항목을 구분해 달라고 요청합니다. 링크가 필요하면 공식 출처를 우선하도록 하고, 모델이 제시한 링크·날짜·수치는 원문에서 다시 확인합니다. 역할 부여나 상세한 문장이 검증을 대신하지는 않습니다.

10. 작은 평가 기준으로 반복 개선하기

첫 답변을 보고 막연히 “더 좋게”라고 요청하기보다 빠진 항목, 불필요한 부분, 잘못된 형식을 구체적으로 되돌려 줍니다. 반복 작업이라면 정확성, 완결성, 형식 준수처럼 짧은 체크리스트로 여러 예시를 시험합니다. OpenAI의 공식 안내도 모든 작업에 통하는 단일 프롬프트는 없다고 설명하며, 실제 입력으로 평가하고 반복해서 다듬을 것을 권합니다.

바로 써보는 프롬프트 조립 순서

다음 순서는 고정 공식이 아니라 빠뜨린 요소를 찾기 위한 선택 기준입니다.

  1. 작업: 무엇을 해달라는 요청인지 적습니다.
  2. 맥락: 독자, 목적, 참고 자료와 기준 시점을 붙입니다.
  3. 기준: 포함·제외 조건과 완료 조건을 적습니다.
  4. 형식: 결과 구조와 필수 필드를 지정합니다.
  5. 검토: 불확실한 부분과 확인할 근거를 따로 표시하게 합니다.

간단한 질문에는 필요한 항목만 쓰면 됩니다. 반대로 중요한 의사결정이나 외부 공개물은 답변 자체를 사실로 간주하지 말고 출처와 원자료를 확인해야 합니다. 이 글의 예시는 실행 결과나 성능 실측값이 아니며, 실제 과제의 성공 여부는 사용한 모델과 입력 자료로 별도 평가해야 합니다.

공식 근거와 확인 범위

2026년 9월 14일에 다음 공식 안내의 현재 내용을 확인했습니다.

  • OpenAI 모델별 프롬프팅 가이드: 명확한 지시, 맥락과 예시, 출력 구조, 평가와 반복 개선
  • Google Gemini 프롬프팅 전략: 구체적인 지시, 제약과 응답 형식, few-shot 예시, 맥락, 작업 분해와 반복
  • Anthropic Claude 프롬프팅 모범 사례: 명확하고 직접적인 지시, 맥락, 예시, 구조와 출력 형식, 결과 확인

제품과 모델의 권장 방식은 바뀔 수 있으므로 이후에는 각 공식 문서의 최신 내용을 재확인해야 합니다.

관련 글

  • AI 챗봇 비교: ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, 당신에게 맞는 선택은?
  • 생성형 AI란 무엇인가? ChatGPT부터 시작하는 AI 입문

이 글의 원문은 좋은 AI 프롬프트 작성법: 원하는 답변을 얻는 10가지 방법 에 있습니다. (Originally published on Briefold)

title: SlicePlanner: Logic-Guided Agentic AI for Online QoS-Aware Network Slicing in Open RAN
description:
arXiv:2611.33664v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Adaptive network slicing in Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) demands reconfiguration decisions that respond to live traffic conditions while remaining safe with respect to Service Level Agreement (SLA) constraints, a combination that purely data-driven controllers cannot reliably guarantee without continuous retraining. We present SlicePlanner, a logic-guided closed-loop framework that treats each RAN reconfiguration as a controlled hypothesis: proposed from live and historical KeyPerformance Indicator (KPI) evidence, filtered through explicit SLA constraints and mined RAN control rules, and committed only when post-action measurements confirm improvement. SlicePlanner comprises two cooperating agents: SliceSense, which monitors live KPIs, retrieves context-conditioned evidence, and ranks candidate RAN actions through a surrogate-guided admissibility filter; and SliceGuard, which validates post-action KPI responses, rolls back harmful configurations, and refreshes rules under distribution drift. Validated over the air using OpenAirInterface, FlexRIC, and commercial Sierra Wireless 5G devices, SlicePlanner reduces SLA latency violations by up to 86% over static slicing and 50% over Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL)-based slicing, while maintaining comparable cell throughput and auditable decisions without online retraining.

title: Nothing Shopify Plus Teardown (Part 2): Mid-to-Late Funnel UX, Community Drop Flows, and High-AOV Checkout Engineering
description:
Many consumer electronics DTC brands survive their initial single-SKU launch only to hit a frustrating conversion plateau in year two. As the catalog expands from one hero product to six or eight variants, storefront conversion rates often drop: shoppers open five tabs trying to compare specs, give up from decision fatigue, and abandon $300–$600 carts in the final ten seconds before checkout.

In Part 1 of our Nothing (nothing.tech) architecture teardown, we examined how sub-brand isolation (CMF by Nothing) and a two-step Story-to-Buy funnel protect top-of-funnel speed. In Part 2, we break down the mid-to-late funnel systems that actually close high-AOV hardware orders: subtractive comparison matrices, lightweight hardware micro-interactions, community co-creation with three-state Drop CTAs, and late-stage checkout trust engineering.

1. Ending Decision Fatigue: The 6-Row Upsell Comparison Matrix

Engineering-led hardware brands frequently copy 40-row factory spec sheets onto their comparison pages. On mobile screens, wide horizontal tables quickly break visual hierarchy and push shoppers to exit.

Nothing's comparison flow (such as across Ear, Ear (a), and Ear (open)) applies strict subtraction—surfacing only the 5 to 7 tangible differences that justify a higher price tier (fit style, ANC depth, wireless charging, high-res audio codecs, battery life, and price).

White Ear and yellow Ear (a). Identify the models before comparing their features. GPT editorial illustration. Source

UX Dimension Typical 3C Spec Sheet Nothing Comparison Pattern Conversion Impact
Row Density 30–40 raw engineering specs 5–7 high-impact buyer differentiators Eliminates choice overload in under 15 seconds
Mobile Layout Wide horizontal scroll table 2-column fixed view + dropdown selector + sticky Buy Now Enables one-handed comparison and immediate upsell
SEO / GEO Readability Flattened comparison JPEG Clean semantic HTML table with highlighted diffs Crawlable by Google and AI answer engines (GEO)

In multi-SKU hardware catalogs, a comparison table is not a user manual—it is an upsell engine. When a shopper immediately sees why an extra $50 unlocks wireless charging and stronger ANC while the sticky Buy Now bar sits at the top of the screen, AOV rises without aggressive popups.

2. Lightweight Hardware Micro-Interactions Without Hurting Core Web Vitals

Selling hardware online means buyers cannot feel chassis weight or tactile buttons. Embedding heavy 3D WebGL viewers directly onto product pages frequently pushes mobile LCP past 5 seconds and degrades INP.

Nothing protects storefront speed by separating storytelling from configuration:

  • Macro imagery and short lazy-loaded loops handle industrial design storytelling on the Story Page.
  • Minimal DOM and pre-fetched swatches keep the Buy Page fast and responsive when shoppers toggle storage tiers and colorways.

The rear Glyph light on the Phone (2a) Plus, from the official product page. Source

3. Beyond Paid Ads: Community Co-Creation & Three-State Drop Flows

Relying purely on paid social creates a fragile linear funnel where orders collapse whenever ad spend pauses. With its 2024 Phone (2a) Plus Community Edition, Nothing turned product development into a four-stage public co-creation cycle—inviting fans to submit and vote on glow-in-the-dark hardware design, wallpapers, packaging, and launch marketing, followed by regional registration flows (including Europe and Japan).

Community members contributed hardware, wallpaper, packaging and campaign designs. GPT editorial illustration. Source

At the storefront level, this pairs with a three-state Drop CTA (Teaser -> Live -> Sold Out Waitlist) so high-intent review traffic never hits a dead-end grey Sold Out button.

WESWOO Reference Implementation (12-Line Shopify Liquid Pattern):

{%- comment -%} WESWOO Example: Three-state Drop CTA driven by Metafield + Variant Stock {%- endcomment -%}
{%- assign stage = product.metafields.custom.drop_stage.value | default: 'live' -%}
{%- assign v = product.selected_or_first_available_variant -%}

{%- if stage == 'teaser' -%}
  <button type="button" data-open-waitlist="early_access">Notify Me — Early Access</button>
{%- elsif v.available -%}
  <button type="submit" name="add">Add to Cart — {{ v.price | money }}</button>
{%- else -%}
  <button type="button" data-open-waitlist="restock" data-variant-id="{{ v.id }}">
    Out of Stock — Notify When Back
  </button>
{%- endif -%}

4. Closing the Final 10 Seconds on $300–$600 Hardware Orders

Before clicking checkout on high-ticket electronics, buyers hesitate over three concerns: upfront sticker shock, accidental damage, and post-purchase support reliability.

Nothing lists Klarna at checkout. Options vary by region. GPT editorial illustration. Source

  1. Upfront Installment Clarity: On key regional storefronts (such as the UK store), Klarna installment messaging appears directly beside pricing rather than hiding at the final payment screen.
  2. One-Click Protection Plans & Accessories: Offering accidental damage coverage or official chargers inside the slide-out cart addresses durability anxiety while adding high-margin AOV.
  3. Top-Navigation Support Transparency: Placing Support, warranty lookup, and software updates prominently in the main header signals long-term brand accountability.

WESWOO Reference Implementation (10-Line Cart Drawer Guard):

{%- comment -%} WESWOO Example: Prevent duplicate or out-of-stock protection plan upsells {%- endcomment -%}
{%- assign plan = all_products['official-protection-plan'] -%}
{%- assign plan_v = plan.first_available_variant -%}
{%- assign in_cart = cart.items | where: 'product_id', plan.id -%}

{%- if plan_v != blank and in_cart.size == 0 -%}
  <div class="ws-cart-upsell">
    <span>Add {{ plan.title | escape }} ({{ plan_v.price | money }})</span>
    <button type="button" data-quick-add="{{ plan_v.id }}">+ Add</button>
  </div>
{%- endif -%}

Practical Engineering Checklist

  1. Lock mobile model comparisons to 2 columns with dropdown switchers, sticky Buy Now bars, and semantic HTML tables.
  2. Keep heavy media on story pages and strip configuration pages down to fast-responding DOM components.
  3. Replace dead-end Sold Out states with variant-aware restock waitlists.
  4. Surface regional installment options, guarded protection-plan upsells, and top-level Support links across the checkout path.

title: How RAG Beats Fine-Tuning: Building a Node.js Company Handbook Simply
description:
A healthtech handbook changes more often than its prose suggests. Product indications, training notes, escalation rules, and approved wording all move on different schedules. That operational constraint changes the answer: retrieve the current, permitted passages at question time instead of teaching those passages to a model through fine-tuning.

TL;DR: RAG usually beats fine-tuning for a company handbook because knowledge stays outside the model. You can replace, delete, date, and permission each source passage, then show the passages used for an answer. Fine-tuning changes model behavior; it is a poor substitute for a mutable content store. Explained simply, RAG looks up changing facts while fine-tuning teaches patterns. For a one-person SaaS, that separation protects the scarce resource: engineering hours that should ship product every week.

The key cost question is not "How many documents do we have?" It is "How many chunks do we embed, retain, search, and re-embed after each edit?" Start with retrieval, measure answer support, and fine-tune later only if repeated behavioral errors remain.

Why doesn't fine-tuning solve a changing handbook?

Fine-tuning and retrieval change different parts of the system. Fine-tuning adjusts a model's parameters from examples. RAG retrieves external text and supplies it as context before generation. The original RAG paper describes this as combining parametric memory with explicit non-parametric memory. That distinction matters more than either acronym.

Facts move.

Suppose an internal healthtech handbook says which product-content claims have completed review. On Tuesday, an editor replaces one approved paragraph. With retrieval, the ingestion job can remove the old chunks, index the new revision, and attach its review state. The generator never needs to memorize that paragraph. With fine-tuning, producing another training set still does not create a reliable document database, a deletion primitive, or a citation trail.

Freshness is only half the issue. Access is part of correctness. A contractor, a support employee, and a clinical reviewer may be allowed to see different passages. Retrieval can filter candidates by authorization metadata before any text enters the model context. Training shared restricted text into model weights makes that boundary harder to reason about. This is an architectural consequence, not a claim that retrieval automatically provides security. The application must enforce it.

I use a simple decision rule: if an editor must be able to change an answer without retraining, the fact belongs in retrieval. If examples are intended to change tone, response shape, or stable task behavior, fine-tuning may be relevant. Many systems eventually use both. They should not use one as a vague replacement for the other.

That is the split.

Build the smallest useful retrieval loop

The first implementation needs four operations: split approved content, embed each chunk, retrieve permitted candidates, and construct a grounded prompt. Keep those boundaries generic. Outsource the undifferentiated embedding and generation work behind interfaces; retain ownership of content state, authorization, and evaluation.

This runnable TypeScript example uses an in-memory index and a deterministic toy embedder. The embedder is deliberately weak, but the retrieval contract, metadata filter, and prompt construction are real. Replace the implementation behind embed when moving beyond the build log.

type Access = "all-staff" | "clinical-review";

type Chunk = {
  id: string;
  documentId: string;
  revision: number;
  access: Access;
  text: string;
  vector: number[];
};

const embed = (text: string): number[] => {
  const vector = Array<number>(64).fill(0);
  for (const token of text.toLowerCase().match(/[a-z0-9]+/g) ?? []) {
    let hash = 0;
    for (const char of token) hash = (hash * 31 + char.charCodeAt(0)) >>> 0;
    vector[hash % vector.length] += 1;
  }
  const norm = Math.hypot(...vector) || 1;
  return vector.map((value) => value / norm);
};

const cosine = (left: number[], right: number[]): number =>
  left.reduce((sum, value, index) => sum + value * right[index], 0);

const source = {
  documentId: "product-content-policy",
  revision: 7,
  access: "all-staff" as const,
  paragraphs: [
    "Publish product content only after its review state is approved.",
    "Archive superseded wording when a new revision becomes active.",
    "Send unresolved medical questions to the clinical review queue."
  ]
};

const index: Chunk[] = source.paragraphs.map((text, position) => ({
  id: `${source.documentId}:r${source.revision}:${position}`,
  documentId: source.documentId,
  revision: source.revision,
  access: source.access,
  text,
  vector: embed(text)
}));

function retrieve(question: string, allowed: Set<Access>, limit = 2): Chunk[] {
  const query = embed(question);
  return index
    .filter((chunk) => allowed.has(chunk.access))
    .map((chunk) => ({ chunk, score: cosine(query, chunk.vector) }))
    .sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score)
    .slice(0, limit)
    .map(({ chunk }) => chunk);
}

function groundedPrompt(question: string, chunks: Chunk[]): string {
  const context = chunks
    .map((chunk) => `[${chunk.id}] ${chunk.text}`)
    .join("\n");

  return [
    "Answer only from the supplied handbook passages.",
    "If they do not support an answer, say that the handbook does not answer it.",
    "Cite passage IDs in the answer.",
    `Question: ${question}`,
    `Passages:\n${context}`
  ].join("\n\n");
}

const question = "What happens to superseded product wording?";
const chunks = retrieve(question, new Set<Access>(["all-staff"]));
console.log(groundedPrompt(question, chunks));

No model call is needed to test this boundary. Inspect the selected IDs first. Generation can hide bad retrieval behind fluent prose, so debugging both at once wastes time.

Start there.

Paragraphs are an acceptable starting unit, not a universal chunking rule. Headings, lists, and tables carry structure that a fixed character window can destroy. Preserve the document ID, revision, section path, access class, and stable chunk ID. Those fields earn their keep during deletion and incident review.

Make index cost an explicit budget

Index growth is multiplicative. Let D be active documents, C the average chunks per document, V the number of separately indexed variants, and R the retained revisions. The stored vector count is approximately D × C × V × R. That equation is intentionally plain. It exposes expensive habits before a vendor bill or a slow rebuild does.

Consider 8,000 active product-content documents averaging 14 chunks. One current variant produces 112,000 vectors. Keeping four complete revisions in the live index produces 448,000. These are arithmetic examples, not benchmark results. The useful decision is to keep one active revision searchable, put history in ordinary archival storage, and delete superseded vectors by stable document and revision identifiers. Do not duplicate the same vector for every role if access can be represented as filterable metadata with identical text. Do create separate chunks when the text itself differs. Measure both choices: heavy metadata filters can reduce the candidate pool available to approximate search, while duplicate indexes increase storage and update work. The right boundary depends on the retrieval engine and permission model. Chunk overlap deserves the same scrutiny. A 20% overlap can create roughly 25% more chunks for long sliding-window documents because each new chunk advances by 80% of its width. That may preserve sentences across boundaries, but it is not free. My initial default would be no overlap for structurally parsed handbook sections; I would add it only where evaluation queries expose boundary misses. This is an explicit trade: lower recurring index work now, with evidence deciding whether more context is worth its permanent storage multiplier.

Track three numbers per ingestion run: active source chunks, inserted vectors, and deleted vectors. Also record the source revision attached to every answer. When those counts disagree with the content system, stop publishing the new index generation. Quiet duplication is a bad use of revenue-per-hour because it raises recurring cost while making freshness ambiguous.

Test the failure modes before adding polish

A demo question is not an evaluation set. Build a small set from real handbook jobs: exact policy lookup, paraphrased lookup, a question spanning two sections, an unauthorized question, a superseded statement, and an unanswerable question. Store expected source IDs or an explicit expectation of no answer.

For retrieval, measure whether an expected passage appears in the first k results. For the final response, verify each material claim against the retrieved passages. A grounded prompt helps, but instructions alone do not guarantee grounded output. Test abstention separately. The correct response to missing evidence is a refusal to invent handbook policy.

Deletion needs a test too. Insert revision 7, replace it with revision 8, and ask the question whose answer changed. Fail the deployment if revision 7 remains retrievable from the active alias. This catches a more dangerous class of bug than an awkward sentence.

Test deletion.

Keep logs useful but sparse: query ID, authorized scope, index generation, retrieved chunk IDs, scores, latency, and answer outcome. Avoid logging raw restricted passages by default. Health information and employee data require their own governance; a semantic-search project does not relax those duties.

Ship the narrow loop. Weekly releases make evaluation drift visible sooner, while a grand ingestion platform can consume a month before anyone learns whether employees ask answerable questions.

What I would change at scale

Move ingestion off the request path first. Content updates should produce an immutable index generation, run retrieval tests against it, and switch an alias only after those tests pass. If the switch fails, the previous generation remains available. The serving path stays boring.

Next, replace the linear scan with an index appropriate to the measured corpus and latency target. Exact search is valuable as an evaluation baseline even after approximate nearest-neighbor search enters production. Approximation trades some recall for speed; compare it against the exact baseline using the same questions and permission filters.

I would also cache embeddings by normalized content hash. An unchanged paragraph should not be embedded merely because an adjacent paragraph changed. The cache must include the embedding configuration in its key, since vectors from incompatible configurations do not belong in the same comparison space.

The trade-off remains clear. Retrieval adds an ingestion pipeline, an index, access filters, and evaluation work. Fine-tuning adds dataset construction, training lifecycle work, and a harder path for changing factual content. For a mutable company handbook, retrieval's operational burden maps directly to the job: find the current allowed text. That is why it wins here. Fine-tuning is still available later for stable behavior that prompt and retrieval evaluation cannot fix.

Sources

  • https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.11401
  • https://owasp.org/www-project-top-10-for-large-language-model-applications/
  • https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/security/index.html

title: How to choose a Bootstrap 5 admin template: a 10-point checklist
description:
Most admin templates look the same in the preview screenshot. The differences show up three weeks into a project, when you try to connect real data, add a language or ship the bundle to a slow phone. This is the checklist I use before committing to one. Every point has a test that takes a few minutes.

Disclosure: I make admin templates (Kova and Kova Lite, linked at the end), so I have opinions about what goes wrong. The checklist works for any template, including mine.

1. Which Bootstrap version, exactly?

"Bootstrap 5" can mean 5.0 from 2021 or the current 5.3. Version 5.3 added native dark mode through data-bs-theme; templates built on older versions usually implement dark mode with their own CSS overrides, which break when you add a Bootstrap component the author did not restyle.

Test: open the bundled bootstrap.min.css and read the version comment on line one.

2. What does it depend on besides Bootstrap?

Look at the <script> tags in the HTML. jQuery, Moment, a chart library, a date picker, a table plugin, an icon font: each is a separate update and a separate security surface. None of them is wrong, but you should know the number before you start.

Test: unzip the template and run grep -rho "<script[^>]*src=[^>]*>" . | sort | uniq -c. A long list is a maintenance bill.

3. How heavy is a single page?

Admin screens load on office laptops and on a phone in a warehouse. Open the dashboard page in Chrome DevTools, Network tab, disable cache, and look at transferred size and the number of requests.

Test: Lighthouse in mobile mode on the main dashboard. You are not chasing 100, only looking for surprises such as a 600 KB chart library to draw four charts.

4. Is the data hard-coded in the HTML?

Many templates ship tables with rows typed into the markup. That is fine for a screenshot and a rewrite for production. Look for templates where tables and charts read from JSON or a single API setting, because that is the part you will replace first.

Test: view source on the orders or users page. If the rows are in the HTML, plan to rebuild the table.

5. Do the interactive parts actually work?

Search boxes that do not search, filters that do not filter, "Export" buttons with no handler. Click everything on the demo, especially tables: sorting, pagination, bulk select, empty states.

Test: sort a numeric column and a date column. Wrong ordering ("100" before "20") means string sorting.

6. Dark mode and RTL, for real

Both are easy to claim and easy to get half right. Switch the demo to dark and open a page with a form, a modal and a chart. Switch to RTL and check the sidebar, dropdown menus and table alignment.

Test: in the demo, toggle dark mode, reload the page. It should stay dark without a flash of light theme.

7. Responsive down to 320 px

Resize the window to 320 px wide. The sidebar should collapse, tables should scroll inside their container rather than the whole page, and no horizontal page scrollbar should appear.

8. Is there a source, or only minified output?

If the template is built from partials or a build step, you will want the source. If it is plain HTML, check that headers and sidebars are not copy-pasted into 40 files by hand, because then every nav change is 40 edits.

Test: look for a src/ or partials/ folder, or a documented build script.

9. License and what it allows

Read the license before the code. Typical questions: can you use it in a client project, in a SaaS you sell, in multiple projects? Marketplace "regular" licenses usually cover one end product. If you are building for clients, check whether each client needs their own license.

10. Documentation and updates

Open the docs page. Good docs cover folder structure, theming, how to add a page, and how data is loaded. Then check the last update date and the changelog; a template untouched for two years will not follow the next Bootstrap release.

Quick scoring

Give each point 0, 1 or 2. Under 12 out of 20, keep looking. Above 16, you probably found something maintainable.

If you want to compare

I built two admin templates on these principles, so you can run the checklist against real ones:

  • Kova Lite: 8 pages, a starter edition. Demo: https://kova-lite.toolsy.pro. Item: https://www.codester.com/items/75045/kova-lite-admin-dashboard-starter-bootstrap-5?ref=toolsy
  • Kova: the full version, 35 pages. Demo: https://kova.toolsy.pro. Item: https://www.codester.com/items/74303/kova-e-commerce-admin-dashboard-bootstrap-5?ref=toolsy

Both use Bootstrap 5.3.3 and vanilla JavaScript with no jQuery, and the charts are a small custom library rather than a third-party package. The data is fictional sample data. I wrote them with AI assistance and tested them by hand. Test them the same way you test any other template, and tell me which points they fail.

title: Disciplined Anthropomorphism: How to Extend Cognitive Language to Artificial Intelligence
description:
arXiv:2611.34090v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Researchers increasingly describe AI in cognitive terms such as "understanding" and "believing", while critics denounce this as wishful anthropomorphism. Both sides align in taking a subsumptive approach, however: they ask whether AI systems fall under concepts minted for human beings, reporting verdicts as discoveries about those systems when they are largely determined by conceptual frames. Yet the problem AI poses is precisely the problem of how to conceptually frame these systems, and the explosive rise of anthropomorphism is best seen as a response to this problem that needs disciplining rather than discouragement. A disciplined anthropomorphism, I argue, should disentangle the inferential connections bundled up in our cognitive concepts and ask which connections to preserve, sever, or forge for AI. The disciplining then comes, on the one hand, from the human conceptual needs that give point to the drawing of these connections and motivate the concepts' extension in the first place; and, on the other hand, from empirical and especially mechanistic evidence that supports and constrains these connections. By reverse-engineering a concept's point in relation to a particular need before re-engineering it to better serve that point in our dealings with AI, anthropomorphizing extensions can be point-based, transposing the work those concepts do for us while revising the inferential workings through which they do it. Transposing human-tailored conceptions of understanding and belief on the pivot of the underlying conceptual needs gives us just the definitional freedom required to accommodate how AI systems differ from us, yielding conceptions that are not just thinned-out versions of existing ones, but potentially richer and better fitted to the peculiarities of AI.

title: 高盛重塑金融数据分析
description:
高盛重塑金融数据分析 (Goldman Sachs Reinventing Financial Data Analytics)

本说明提取了关于资本市场运营模型、金融数据产品、盘中与历史数据、自助式分析、机器学习、混合云、AWS 服务以及企业 FSI（金融服务业）治理的实用经验。

高管学习重点 (Executive learning)

核心经验是，企业金融数据的现代化，既是一个数据产品和运营模型的问题，也是一个技术问题。 一个实用的平台必须汇集大量市场数据、历史保真度、证券和衍生品模型、一致的证券主数据、数据权限、目录化、分析、笔记本、量化库、机器学习，以及发布结果的受控路径。

演示文稿描述了一种交易大厅模型：销售人员产生想法并服务客户，交易员分析市场、执行交易同时管理风险，工程师架构和运营技术，而量化分析师 (quants) 则分析数据、开发策略并管理模型。 一个成功的平台应该让这些团队能够协同合作，而不必强迫每个团队重新解决数据身份、权限、时间序列重建或运营控制等问题。

最强烈的架构主题是“受控的自助服务”。 研究人员应该能够发现、查询、连接、分析和共享受治理的数据，而无需开启未受控的敏感或授权信息副本。 最强烈的控制主题则是：访问权限、数据血缘 (lineage)、有效时间 (valid time)、交易时间 (transaction time)、更正处理及审计能力，必须在数据产品设计之初就纳入，而不是在分析完成后才添加。

最强烈的现代化主题是“混合云采用”。 云服务可以提供精选数据 (curated data)、弹性分析、笔记本、回测、机器学习和数据产品发布，同时现有的本地 (on-premises) 资产继续拥有特定的执行、投资组合或低延迟功能。 来源并未展示实时的交易集成，因此云端分析平台不应被呈现为订单管理或交易所连接系统。

交易大厅运营模型 (Trading-floor operating model)

该来源将资本市场交易大厅划分为四个互补的用户群体。 销售团队产生想法、负责客户并管理关系。 交易员分析市场、执行交易并管理风险。 工程师设计解决方案架构、开发应用程序并管理基础设施。 量化分析师分析数据、开发策略并管理模型。 这种划分非常有用，因为它清楚表明数据平台必须在保留职责分离的同时，服务于业务和技术职责。

示例中的量化研究问题是：投资于折价交易的高质量股票是否会跑赢大盘。 这是一个假设，需要对质量、估值、投资范围、数据可用日期、交易成本、基准和风险进行定义。 这并不是高盛报告的结果或建议。 其价值在于说明数据平台如何支持从原始证据到测试，再到可能投入生产环境的研究问题。

演示文稿描述了从研究到生产的四个阶段方法。 设置 (Setup) 部署基础设施并获取数据。 开发 (Development) 创建策略并优化回测。 分析 (Analysis) 比较指标并运行场景。 生产化 (Productionization) 执行交易并监控风险。 实际的生产实施应在这些阶段中加入明确的模型审批、数据质量网关、权限检查、变更管理、交易前控制、对账、监控、事件响应和交易后审查。

这些角色和生命周期暗示了一种责任共担模型。 量化分析师需要快速实验，但工程师需要可重复性和可观测性。 交易员需要及时的信息，但风险职能部门需要独立的控制。 销售和客户团队需要经过审批的数据产品，但许可和机密性限制必须保持可执行。 数据平台应在其权限、界面、审计记录和审批工作流中展现这些职责。

数据平台架构 (Data-platform architecture)

演示文稿将数据平台分为“分析层”以及“数据建模与集成层”。 分析层运行并行化的量化分析任务，并直接在笔记本环境中支持进一步的研究。 数据建模与集成层包含证券和衍生品的数据模型以及集中的数据目录。 这种分离是一种有用的设计模式，因为它区分了计算规模与研究人员体验，以及受治理的语义模型与数据探索。

成熟的平台还应将原始源数据、标准化数据、参考数据、精选数据产品、衍生特征、模型输出与审计工件分开。 每一层都应保留来源血缘、转换历史、时间戳、质量状态、所有权、保留期限和权限。 研究人员可以使用精选产品，而无需获得对每个原始来源的无限制访问权，而审计或控制职能部门可能需要重建从原始数据到结果的路径。

集中式数据建模在资本市场中尤为重要，因为相同的证券、衍生品、指数、发行人、账户或公司事件可能出现在许多源标识符下。 共享模型应定义标识符、工具类型、货币、结算、日历、公司行动、来源优先顺序和更正策略。 它还应说明在不破坏现有分析的情况下，如何引入新工具和新数据供应商。

数据目录应描述数据集的含义、所有者、新鲜度、涵盖的市场和字段、允许的使用方式、通过的质量检查以及它与其他产品的关联。 对于受监管的研究环境而言，仅存储数据表名称的目录是不够的。 研究人员需要语义定义，而控制职能部门需要血缘和权限证据。

Tick 数据库与市场数据规模 (Tick database and market-data scale)

演示文稿描述了一个针对金融市场访问模式的内存时间序列数据库。 它声称该存储系统能够以毫秒级延迟，每秒处理数百万种证券的数千次更新。 示例记录包含时间、买价 (bid)、卖价 (ask) 和 TRD（总回报差异，Total Return Difference）。 页面还声称每个代码每秒可达 50 万条记录的高吞吐量写入，可水平扩展至 PB 级别，采用无模式 (schema-less) 存储，并具备 ACID 事务特性。

这些数字和特征是演示文稿的断言，而非本地基准测试证据。 不同的吞吐量描述并非完整的容量规格，且无模式存储与 ACID 事务的结合并未加以解释。 企业团队必须厘清该声明是指单一代码、单一节点、集群、分区、数据馈送 (feed) 还是基准测试工作负载；更新是插入还是更正；适用哪些持久性保证；以及正在测量哪个百分位数的延迟。

生产环境的 Tick 存储必须定义事件时间、摄取时间、交易时间、序列号、更正消息、迟到数据、乱序消息、重复项、快照、保留、重放和恢复。 它应区分交易 (trade) 与报价 (quote)、指示性价值与可执行报价，以及更正与新市场事件。 存储和计算的选择应由查询模式、延迟、保留期、吞吐量、容错性以及重现历史状态的需求来驱动。

来源建议使用 AWS Lambda 进行按需部署，Amazon CloudWatch 进行日志记录，HashiCorp Nomad 进行流程编排，以及 Amazon DynamoDB 处理集群元数据。 这是一个建议的服务映射，而不是已部署的架构。 未包含 Lambda 函数、Nomad 任务规格、DynamoDB 模式、CloudWatch 仪表板、自动扩展策略、故障策略或性能测试。

金融数据建模挑战 (Financial-data modeling challenges)

演示文稿解释了为何金融数据难以建模。 研究人员可能从有限的样本开始，接着摄取并解析数百个文件，浏览不一致的数据字典，重新映射历史格式变更，解读 PDF 手册，将记录映射到标准模型，连接多个来源，执行技术和语义检查，并建立持续的质量反馈循环。

这些不仅仅是数据工程上的不便。 不一致的字段定义会改变因子或风险衡量指标。 历史格式的改变会在时间序列中产生虚假的断层。 PDF 的解读错误会误报合同条款。 使用错误标识符进行的连接 (Join) 会附加错误的价格或发行人。 缺失发布时间戳会造成前视偏差 (look-ahead bias)。 质量循环应同时包含机器检查和领域所有者的审查。

技术检查应涵盖模式、数据类型、范围、空值、重复项、时间戳、序列连续性、引用完整性、货币和单位一致性。 语义检查应涵盖价格在经济上是否合理、公司行动是否已反映、衍生品的标的物和乘数是否正确、估值日期是否有效，以及来源的业务含义是否与规范模型相符。

数据质量应受到测量并与数据产品一起发布。 消费者应能看到新鲜度、完整性、准确性指标、已知事件、更正状态以及负责的所有者。 不应仅因为流水线在没有技术错误的情况下完成，就认为结果具备权威性。

数据发布与权限模型 (Data distribution and entitlement model)

来源描述了在数据集、行 (row) 和字段 (field) 级别强制执行的数据权限。 权限定义了哪些用户或系统可以访问数据以及他们可以做什么（例如查看或修改）。 它还描述了细化至单个单元格的控制、基于角色、位置、时间和设备的上下文感知，以及提供访问透明度与控制的治理。

基于角色的访问控制 (RBAC) 根据用户的工作或角色分配权限。 基于属性的访问控制 (ABAC) 评估部门、位置或其他策略上下文等属性。 用户特定授权直接将访问权分配给个人。 企业平台可能同时使用这三种方法，但应定义优先级、拒绝行为、审批、到期、紧急访问和审计日志，以便例外情况不会在不知不觉中覆盖更广泛的控制措施。

细粒度的授权在金融数据中尤为重要。 用户可能被允许查看证券的公开价格，但不能查看客户仓位、专有的研究字段、授权供应商的属性，或未经审批的衍生信号。 可以共享数据集进行分析，同时某些行或列仍受限制。 系统应在每个访问路径强制执行策略，包括笔记本、API、SQL、下载、导出、缓存、物化视图 (materialized views) 和机器学习任务。

上下文访问应被视为控制输入，而非明确数据所有者的替代品。 决策可能取决于用户的角色、位置、设备状态、时间、网络、目的以及所请求字段的敏感度。 策略决策、策略版本、请求身份、结果和原因都应可供审计。

精选数据与证券主数据 (Curated data and Security Master)

第二个主题介绍了高盛与 AWS 在云端中发现、组织和分析金融数据的合作。 提议的精选数据产品包括高盛精选的盘中和日终市场数据、通过 AWS Data Exchange 获取的第三方产品、高盛专有数据、数千种证券/指数/金融产品的双时态 (bi-temporal) 数据、一致的标识符，以及选定资产超过 30 年的标准化历史。

这些是本地演示文稿的主张，应如实标注。 该仓库不包含精选数据馈送、权限配置、数据合同、源数据集、基准测试，或对历史长度和工具覆盖范围的独立验证。 内部的学习价值在于产品概念：消费者应接收具有一致含义、历史、身份和访问权的机构治理数据，而不是一堆脱节的供应商文件。

高盛证券主数据 (Security Master) 被描述为跨多个数据源的一致性框架。 以企业术语来说，证券主数据解决了跨证券、指数、衍生品、发行人、公司事件和供应商代码的身份解析问题。 它应提供稳定的内部标识符、源映射、生效日期、工具属性、公司行动关联和更正历史。

证券主数据必须被视为受治理的控制产品。 它应支持新工具的引入、合同条款的变更、合并、拆股、剥离、退市、多种股份类别、到期的衍生品以及来源分歧。 每个映射决策都应该是可追溯的。 消费者应该知道模型或报告中使用了哪个标识符，以及该映射是否随后被更正。

演示文稿列举了板块与子板块分类，以及跟踪由股票拆分和合并引起的代码变更，作为精选数据价值的示例。 这些示例展示了参考数据质量如何同时支持研究和运营。 错误的分类会扭曲因子或投资组合的敞口，而错误的代码映射会将价格、仓位或公司事件附加到错误的证券上。

双时态与盘中数据 (Bi-temporal and intraday data)

盘中 (Intraday) 部分强调价格是实时变动的，时间表在纳秒分辨率下可能是稀疏的，必须以低延迟提供最新的数据，更新必须在有效时间和交易时间上保持幂等性 (idempotent)，并且必须实时支持乱序回填与更正。 报告指出每秒 1000 万次更新、超过 2500 万种资产以及 150 个市场。 这些值是来源报告的规模主张，没有本地的基准测试或日期。

有效时间 (Valid time) 是事实在现实世界中为真的时间。 交易时间 (Transaction time) 是事实被记录或系统知道的时间。 双时态数据保留了这两条时间线，允许分析师询问“在特定时间什么是真的”以及“系统在特定时间知道什么”。 这种区分对于回测、调查、审计、估值和监管审查至关重要。

价格可能在某个市场时间戳是有效的，但却迟到了。 公司行动可能在某个日期生效，但却在另一个日期输入系统。 供应商可能在原始观察后修改记录。 双时态存储必须保留原始记录、更正、有效期间、记录期间、原因和来源。 幂等处理必须确保重放相同事件不会产生重复的经济事实。

日终数据 (End-of-day data) 通常只捕获收盘价，无法重建盘中状态。 这对于某些报告和较低频率的模型可能有用，但当研究问题取决于盘中条件时，它无法取代报价、交易、成交量、事件和更正历史记录。 平台应说明每个数据产品的时间粒度和可用性。

历史重建应同时支持回测和事件分析。 研究人员可能需要最新修正的历史视图，而调查人员可能需要交易员在做出决策时可获得的视图。 这是不同的查询，绝不能混为一谈。

量化分析与研究人员体验 (Quantitative analytics and researcher experience)

演示文稿描述了通过现值变动、交互式市场分析、笔记本、GS Quant、Amazon FinSpace 以及时间序列数据平台进行的量化分析。 现值是未来现金流以估计的回报率折现后的当前价值。 这个例子强调了在比较投资或计算风险时，分析定义、利率、日历和数据版本的重要性。

GS Quant 被描述为一个开源的 Python 量化工具包，可在 pandas 中访问 500 多个数据集、100 多个时间序列分析函数，并提供 SDK API 以检索定价和风险信息。 本地页面链接到高盛 gs-quant GitHub 仓库，但不包含本地安装、代码、版本、测试或集成。 这些功能应作为引用的产品描述，而不是可用的本地实现。

研究人员的体验包括用于交互式市场分析的 PlotTool Pro、用于探索的笔记本、用于量化函数的 GS Quant、FinSpace 托管的笔记本和计算，以及时间序列数据平台。 一个好的工作台应让用户能够快速探索，同时保留重现结果所需的数据快照、代码、参数、模型版本和输出血缘。

演示文稿将图计算与缓存描述为功能性的，每个节点具有并行执行和数据缓存。 这暗示了一个依赖图 (dependency graph)，在其中衍生分析可以并行计算，中间结果可以重复使用。 生产设计必须指定缓存键、失效、数据版本依赖性、新鲜度、内存限制、持久性、访问控制以及源更正后的行为。

采用 Legend 的金融数据产品生命周期 (Financial-data product lifecycle with Legend)

FINOS Legend 参考资料以自助服务生命周期进行总结。 治理 (CURATE) 描述并连接数据。 查找 (FIND) 定位有意义的数据。 检索 (RETRIEVE) 通过简单的访问路径查询它。 共享 (SHARE) 转换并分发它。 分析 (ANALYZE) 支持实验与调查。 治理 (GOVERN) 将质量和控制内置于数据产品中。 这个词汇库作为金融数据目录的运营模型非常有用。

真正的实施需要将所有权和控制附加到每个生命周期活动上。 数据治理需要规范模型、源映射、质量检查和管理员。 查找需要可搜索的元数据与具备权限感知的结果。 检索需要查询授权、新鲜度、成本和审计。 共享需要许可和目的控制。 分析需要隔离的工作区和可重现性。 治理需要血缘、保留期、事件管理、模型风险以及策略被强制执行的证据。

来源并未展示 FINOS Legend 部署、目录记录、血缘图、策略决策或物化 API。 本地课程应将生命周期呈现为一个有用的概念框架，而非证明该仓库包含 Legend 服务的证据。

金融云、Redshift 与 SageMaker 工作流 (Financial Cloud, Redshift, and SageMaker workflow)

页面描述了用于时间序列数据管理与分析的高盛金融云，并探讨如何将其与 Amazon Redshift 及基于 Twitter 的加密货币每日情绪分析用例相结合。 研究问题是：近期情绪和当前市场状况是否能帮助预测短期回报是正还是负。

提议的“改造前”流程获取内部和第三方数据，将时间序列数据汇入 Amazon Redshift，执行关系型和机器学习分析，并将预测结果带回高盛金融云。 Amazon Data Exchange 被指定为来源，Amazon SageMaker 为机器学习服务。 演示文稿称 Redshift 为 PB 级无服务器分析解决方案，但未提供模式、工作负载、规模、延迟、成本或准确性的基准测试。

该工作流针对单个数据集建模，并在 Redshift 中物化金融云的精选数据。 接着，它创建一个结合市场基本面和情绪的组合数据集，使用 ML 模型输出的正负回报预测来扩展该数据集，查询并查看结果，并在满意后，指示 Legend 将组合数据集物化回金融云中。 分析师随后可以通过 PlotTool Pro 审问精选的时间序列。

这是演示文稿中最清晰的端到端数据产品模式。 它分离了来源摄取、分析建模、特征和预测生成、结果审查、受治理的发布以及分析师消费。 本地仓库不包含 SQL、Redshift 数据表、SageMaker 模型、训练数据、评估指标、Legend 调用、物化任务或结果，因此该流程是概念性的，无法重现。

生产环境的 ML 工作流需要时间点 (point-in-time) 的特征存储、标签定义、训练和验证拆分、数据泄漏控制、模型版本控制、可解释性、校准、漂移监控、审批和回滚 (rollback)。 情绪特征需要源许可、时间戳对齐、语言和重复处理，以及在考虑了市场和基本面因子后，它能贡献增量信息的证据。

Tick 数据、TRD 与均值回归 (Tick data, TRD, and mean reversion)

演示文稿介绍了 TRD 作为总回报差异 (Total Return Difference)，并将其与均值回归 (mean-reversion) 交易关联起来。 教学示例是投资高度相关配对中表现不佳的资产，期望它相对于同行能表现出众。 均值回归假设极端偏离历史平均值的状况最终可能会收敛，但这并不是价格会自我修正的保证。

页面描述了超买和超卖情况，并提到相对强弱指数 (RSI) 是介于 0 到 100 之间的动能震荡指标。 它将高于 70 的值与超买情况相关联，将低于 30 的值与超卖情况相关联。 这些阈值是常见的教学惯例，而非通用的交易规则。 生产策略必须定义投资范围、回溯期、配对选择、对冲比例、持有期、成本、止损，以及该关系不再有效的条件。

当关系破裂、结构性事件改变工具、流动性消失、趋势持续，或者价格差距反映的是新信息而非暂时的失衡时，均值回归可能会失败。 高度相关的配对在压力下可能变得更具相关性，或急剧背离。 监控应包括价差稳定性、相关性、因子敞口、流动性、融券、事件风险和最大回撤 (drawdown)。

风险维度交易与投资组合分布 (Trading in Risk Dimensions and portfolio distributions)

演示文稿将“在风险维度中交易”描述为使用蒙特卡洛模拟 (Monte Carlo simulation) 和 ASA 重要性抽样 (importance sampling)，在多元市场中分析投资组合级别的分布。 其三层外壳结构包含：用于将交易规则调整为传入市场数据的内壳；用于风险指标和策略的中壳；以及用于使用自适应模拟退火 (ASA) 进行全局优化的外壳。

内壳与调整交易规则和典型动能指标相关。 中壳衡量风险和策略行为。 外壳将交易系统拟合至历史数据，并跨投资组合进行优化。 这些术语是来源的描述，而不是实现规格。 未提供任何代码、参数设置、数据集、收敛标准或验证结果。

重要性抽样是一种在目标分布下估计期望值的方法，通过从更方便的提议分布 (proposal distribution) 中抽样并应用权重来实现。 如果目标密度为 p，提议密度为 q，样本会获得与 p 除以 q 成正比的权重，前提是满足必要的支撑集 (support) 和可积性条件。 当直接的蒙特卡洛需要太多一般样本时，这可以提高罕见事件或尾部估计的效率。

当提议权重高度集中，或提议未涵盖目标的重要部分时，重要性抽样也可能产生不稳定的估计。 生产环境的风险引擎应监控有效样本数、权重集中度、收敛性、对提议选择的敏感度以及可重现性。 蒙特卡洛和 ASA 是风险分析工具，不能证明策略会产生回报或优化器已找到全局最优的投资组合。

运营敏捷性与性能经验 (Operating agility and performance lessons)

来源指出，典型的一天可能包括跨 500 种工具的数百万次交易、1,500 次代码发布以及 PB 级的分析数据。 这些数字是报告的演示文稿背景，没有测量日期或支持记录。 尽管如此，它们说明了为何资本市场平台必须结合高吞吐量数据、快速部署、量化实验和强大的控制。

该页面确定了三个教训。 可用性意味着在构建时将操作员的简单性铭记在心。 风险管理意味着支持混合运营，而不是假设每个功能都必须迁移到云端。 性能意味着及早考虑网络特性。 这些教训比数字主张更持久，因为它们解决了技术选择如何影响交易员、量化分析师、工程师和控制措施的问题。

操作员的简单性并不意味着消除治理。 简单的用户体验应隐藏不必要的基础设施复杂性，同时显示数据新鲜度、权限、质量、模型版本、成本和审批状态。 混合风险管理需要在本地和云端边界明确划分头寸、订单、成交、现金、参考数据、分析和限额的所有权。 网络设计在平台被承诺之前，必须考虑数据移动、查询局部性、延迟、吞吐量、故障和数据驻留。

AWS 服务映射 (AWS service mapping)

高盛的页面命名了 AWS Data Exchange、AWS PrivateLink、Amazon Route 53、AWS Lambda、Amazon CloudWatch、AWS Glue 和 AWS Secrets Manager，围绕着数据采购与分发。 合理的解释是，Data Exchange 可以提供第三方数据产品，PrivateLink 可以支持私有连接，Route 53 可以提供服务发现或 DNS，Lambda 可以处理有边界的事件驱动任务，CloudWatch 可以提供日志和指标，Glue 可以支持目录或转换，而 Secrets Manager 可以保护连接密钥。 该页面未包含订阅、网络配置、函数、任务、策略、仪表板或密钥，因此这是一个建议的服务映射，而不是确认的部署。

提议使用 Amazon Redshift 对结合时间序列、基本面和情绪数据进行关系型与机器学习分析。 提议使用 Amazon SageMaker 用于工作流的 ML 部分。 Amazon FinSpace 被命名为金融分析和笔记本环境。 应根据工作负载、数据所有权、延迟、访问模型、成本和运营责任来选择这些服务。 没有任何单一的命名服务可以取代对规范数据模型、证券主数据、目录、权限层和审计轨迹的需求。

外围的 FSI 材料建议使用 Amazon S3 进行持久存储，AWS DataSync 和 S3 File Gateway 进行混合移动，S3 跨区域复制和生命周期策略以实现持久性和成本控制，Amazon EFS 用于共享文件，FSx for Lustre 用于高吞吐量工作负载，以及使用 Airflow 或其他编排工具处理大型任务。 它还提到了 QuickSight 用于仪表板，以及 SageMaker 用于 AI 和 ML。 这些是一般的 FSI 选项，而不是直接的高盛实现证据。

相邻的因子和宏观材料提出了 S3 Vectors、Bedrock、Nova、Apache Iceberg 或 S3 Tables、具备 Managed kdb Insights 的 FinSpace、ClickHouse、InfluxDB、Batch、Step Functions、HPC ParallelCluster、Elastic Fabric Adapter、Nitro 系统、增强型网络以及 PrivateLink。 这些服务扩展了更广泛的沉浸式学习日 (immersion-day) 研究叙事，但高盛页面本身明确展示的只有结合其金融云和数据产品使用 Redshift 和 SageMaker 的 ML 工作流。

混合现代化与迁移 (Hybrid modernization and migration)

原始的规划笔记指出，买方 (buy-side) 客户通常已经拥有自己的基础设施，可能不希望将运营和执行移至公有云。 AWS 被定位为分析师的工具包、研究环境，以及改进数据和决策工作流的方法。 这与高盛页面中“混合模式是风险管理的一部分”的教训是一致的。

相邻的迁移材料描述了绞杀榕模式 (Strangler Fig pattern)。 评估会发现应用程序和依赖关系。 试点移动一个非关键的小组件。 重构逐步以云服务取代单体架构 (monolithic) 组件。 监控测量行为并指导调整。 切换只有在验证了替换后才转移流量。 这是一般的迁移指南，而非高盛专属的项目计划，但对企业采用很有用。

迁移参考资料点名了 Application Discovery Service 用于依赖分析，EC2、Lambda、API Gateway 和 RDS 作为设计选项，Database Migration Service 用于数据移动，Elastic Beanstalk 或 ECS 用于部署，Elastic Load Balancing 进行流量分配，CloudWatch 用于监控，Snowball 用于大型传输，Outposts 满足混合需求，AWS Backup 进行备份，以及冗余的本地系统用于回滚。 这些服务应通过工作负载和控制评估来选择，而不是作为清单来采用。

FSI 迁移考量包括数据安全与合规性、数据主权、性能与延迟、成本管理、停机时间、数据丢失、安全漏洞以及与传统系统的集成。 企业项目应维持经过验证的回滚路径、冗余系统、演练环境、备份、监控和警报、对账，以及明确的切换验收标准。

安全、治理与可审计性 (Security, governance, and auditability)

目标页面最强烈的治理主张是数据集、行和字段级别的权限；基于角色、属性和用户的授权；集中式目录化；双时态历史；技术和语义检查；以及质量反馈循环。 对于生产环境，这些控制应通过“策略即代码 (policy-as-code)”或等效的可强制执行控制来实现，而不仅仅是通过文档说明。

相邻的 FSI 参考资料增加了端到端加密、静态加密、基于角色的访问控制、最小权限原则、临时 IAM 角色凭证、明确的 IAM 策略、基础设施即代码、自动恢复、跨区域复制、生命周期管理、混合文件访问，以及经过测试的灾难恢复。 它还讨论了数据传输、EFS、FSx for Lustre、Airflow、监控和备份。 这些是建议的企业控制和背景，不是高盛页面实现它们的证据。

数据治理应记录所有者、分类、保留期、许可、驻留位置、血缘、新鲜度、质量状态、允许的使用方式以及消费者权限。 物化的数据产品必须保留其来源和转换历史。 模型结果必须保留特征快照、代码或模型版本、训练期间、评估结果、审查者以及发布决策。 查询或下载必须可归因于某个用户或服务身份。

机密、密钥、凭证和网络路径应与应用程序代码分开管理。 对专有高盛数据、第三方授权数据、客户信息、研究和模型输出的访问必须限制在特定目的。 能分析精选产品的用户，不应自动拥有导出原始授权数据或更改规范来源的权限。

监控与监管韧性 (Surveillance and regulatory resilience)

相邻的 FSI 材料将交易监控描述为收集审计轨迹和市场数据、挖掘威胁场景，并针对操纵、扭曲、违反规则、非法交易、欺诈、人为定价以及滥用信息产生警报。 金融数据平台应使源数据、转换、分析师决策、模型输出、发布产品以及与交易相关的消费者，对适当的监控和审计职能部门保持可见性。

该参考资料讨论了监管系统合规性与完整性 (Reg SCI) 的期望，涉及容量、完整性、韧性、可用性、安全性、业务连续性和灾难恢复、第三方供应商中断、未经授权的访问、拒绝服务攻击，以及入侵处理或通知。 适用性取决于实体、活动、司法管辖区和系统边界。 高盛页面不是交易所级别的实现，也没有建立 Reg SCI 合规性。

该参考资料报告了说明性的规模值：大约每天 0.5 万亿条消息、不到 20 微秒的整合市场数据延迟、约 35 微秒的订单处理、每天约 10 TB 的压缩实时数据、约 300 种威胁场景，以及约 25 个数据源。 这些数字是相邻参考资料的主张，而非高盛数据平台的测量值。 它们仅应被用来构建规模、延迟、审计和韧性问题的框架。

具有韧性的数据平台必须支持重放、更正、对账、受控降级、依赖故障、区域故障、网络分区、供应商中断以及数据质量事件响应。 日终处理应更新并验证交易，核对记录，产生损益 (P&L) 和按市值计价 (mark-to-market) 报告，将数据归档，并为下一个运营周期做准备。 系统必须保留已知内容、更改内容、审批更改者以及如何通知消费者的证据。

外部与演示文稿主张 (External and presentation claims)

高盛页面指出，其金融云降低了复杂金融数据管理的门槛，释放了技术和量化资源，通过经过市场考验的数据和近乎实时的分析加快了上市时间，通过云原生服务支持全球交易业务，并保留了模块化的成本控制。 这些是价值主张。 本地仓库并未提供成本比较、采用率衡量、生产力研究、服务水平报告或独立的基准测试。

页面声称以毫秒级延迟每秒对数百万种证券进行数千次更新，每个代码每秒 50 万次写入，PB 级规模，每秒 1000 万次更新，超过 2500 万种资产，150 个市场，跨 500 种工具的数百万次交易，1500 次代码发布，以及 PB 级的分析数据。 这些主张缺乏日期、工作负载定义、测量方法、百分位数定义以及支持工件。 它们必须被标记为演示文稿报告的数字，而不是经过验证的平台规格。

页面链接至 gs data、Goldman Marquee、FINOS Legend 和 gs-quant。 如果重复使用它们的产品描述和外部功能，应将其引用为外部参考，而非作为本地实现事实来呈现。 关于 S3、EKS、RDS、托管 Kafka、GPU 计算、YellowDog、多区域架构以及更快的策略交付的随附 QRT 故事，是独立的客户或合作伙伴参考，不应被用来填补高盛架构的空白。

相邻的因子和宏观页面包含关于 400 多个因子、98% 替代数据调查、GenAI 生成的 alpha、正利润期、Brain 和 LikeFolio 以及非线性市场推理的进一步主张。 这些不是高盛数据平台的证据，应与本知识库保持明确的分离。

内部采用路线图 (Internal adoption roadmap)

企业团队可以从定义规范的证券和衍生品模型、受治理的来源目录、数据质量框架以及权限模型开始。 最初的产品应暴露一个小型、高价值、特定时间点 (point-in-time) 的精选数据集，其中包含所有权、血缘、新鲜度、更正历史以及记录在案的允许用途。 这会产生价值，而不会产生实时的执行依赖。

下一个阶段是研究人员工作台，配备笔记本、经审批的量化库、查询访问权、可重现的环境以及衍生产品的受控物化。 每项分析都应保留代码、参数、数据快照、模型版本和输出血缘。 缓存和并行执行应能提高可用性，但不应使得当源数据变更时结果无法失效。

接着是双时态盘中与历史平台。 它应处理有序和乱序事件、更正、迟到数据以及重放。 该平台应同时支持最新修正的历史记录以及“当时已知”的历史记录。 在数据暴露给风险或模型用户之前，证券主数据应核对标识符、公司事件和工具属性。

下一阶段是受控的 Redshift 和 SageMaker（或等效）的 ML 工作流。 特征和标签应该具有时间点特性，模型应该进行版本控制和验证，预测应该带有置信度和漂移状态，发布回精选金融数据层应需要审查。 模型输出应该是可分析的数据产品，而不是隐含的交易指令。

只有在数据产品、身份、权限、质量、血缘、韧性和模型治理得到证明之后，机构才应考虑与风险、投资组合或执行系统进行更广泛的集成。 这些集成需要确定性控制、单一事实来源所有权、对账、监控、审批、回滚以及经过测试的降级运营。

最终内部总结 (Final internal takeaway)

该演示文稿最有价值的用途，是作为构建受治理的资本市场数据产品的蓝图。 一个成功的平台结合了一致的证券主数据、双时态和盘中历史、集中式目录、细粒度权限、质量反馈、可扩展的分析、笔记本和量化工具、机器学习工作流，以及受控地发布回受信任数据层的能力。

该平台应能加快研究速度，而不会削弱控制力。 它应该支持自助服务但不允许不受控的数据复制，支持混合运营但不会导致系统所有权模糊，并支持云端规模但不会混淆吞吐量主张与生产就绪状态。 它应允许量化分析师、交易员、工程师、销售、风险、合规和运营部门使用相同的、受治理的事实，同时保留每个角色的不同权限和责任。

本地证据支持了教育性的架构和运营模型讨论。 它不支持高盛同时部署了每个命名的 AWS 服务、达到了每个声明的容量、测量出具体的成本降低、改善了投资回报，或完全按照描述实施了监管控制的主张。 内部团队应将这些想法作为设计输入，并在将其采纳为技术、风险、采购或投资结论之前，要求提供独立的证据。

title: PeerReveal: Learning to Generalize in AI Peer Review Detection
description:
arXiv:2611.33555v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Can we distinguish fully AI-generated reviews from those using AI only to rewrite human judgement? Furthermore, can we do so reliably when reviews are generated from diverse AI models and workflows across scientific domains? To this end, we introduce PeerReveal, a new detector that grounds its decisions in learned relationships between a review's claims and reference claims drawn from AI-generated reviews of the same paper, complemented by review-level textual signals. We evaluate PeerReveal on PeerShift, a new, challenging test set of 5,430 reviews spanning multiple domains, including machine learning, life sciences, and social sciences, combining variation in disciplinary review conventions with diverse AI review-production mechanisms. With regular training, PeerReveal achieves 70.52% pooled Macro-F1 on this benchmark, improving over the strongest baseline by 11.48 points. We develop an effective and practical adversarial training framework that further improves the detector's generalization using a small local generator optimized to produce challenging reviews, raising pooled Macro-F1 from 70.52% to 82.40%. These results show that robust AI-review detection benefits from richer review-level evidence and adversarial training on more challenging generation processes.

title: Under the Hood of Google Cloud Data Agent Kit: MCP Tools, SKILL.md Playbooks & Custom Guardrails
description:
Welcome !

In Part 1, we set up Google Cloud Data Agent Kit (DAK) in Antigravity IDE and stayed mostly on the UI side that looked at browsing Cloud Storage, previewing BigQuery tables, and running inline SQL through the Mini Cloud Console.

Remember that two-lane architecture from Part 1?

  • Lane 1 (IDE UI) talks to Google Cloud over direct Cloud APIs so browsing tables and schemas is instant and burns zero LLM tokens.

  • Lane 2 (AI Coding Agent) is where the real automation happens - combining MCP Tools and Agentic Skills (SKILL.md).

When people hear Agentic Skills or MCP, it can easily sound like black-box buzzwords. In this post, we're going to open the hood in Antigravity IDE, see what Google Cloud engineers actually put inside a SKILL.md file, and then put both MCP tools and Skills to work on our devfest_commerce dataset.

Why Giving an LLM Raw Database Access Isn't Enough

Giving an AI coding assistant an MCP connection to BigQuery solves context, it can read your live schemas instead of guessing table and column names.

But live access alone doesn't make an agent a good data engineer. Without guidance, a general-purpose model will still happily:

  • Write SELECT * on a 10 TB table
  • Use slower WHERE id IN (SELECT ...) subqueries instead of WHERE EXISTS
  • Skip partition filters or cluster keys
  • Run a DROP TABLE or TRUNCATE without double-checking if you phrase a cleanup prompt loosely

That is the gap between connecting an agent to your data and teaching it how to work safely and efficiently with Google Data Cloud.

Hands vs. Brains: MCP Tools vs. Agentic Skills

Data Agent Kit splits that responsibility into two clean pieces:

  • MCP Tools ("The Hands"): Live Model Context Protocol connectors that let the agent call Google Cloud APIs - listing datasets, reading table schemas, inspecting Cloud Storage objects, or executing queries - without you copy-pasting metadata into chat.

  • Agentic Skills ("The Brains"): Plain, open-source Markdown files (SKILL.md) written by Google Cloud engineers. They contain explicit rules, decision trees, and checklists for specific workflows like BigQuery SQL optimization, data cleaning, dbt/Dataform pipelines, Spark debugging, and data-loss prevention.

Step 1: Ask the Agent What It Actually Has Enabled

Before digging into files, try this exact prompt I ran during my DevFest Mangaluru demo inside the Antigravity Agent Chat panel:

What Data Agent Kit skills and MCP tools do you currently have enabled for BigQuery and Cloud Storage? Group them briefly into "Skills (Playbooks)" and "MCP Tools (Actions)" so we can see how you work.

You will see the agent separate its actions (MCP tools for inspecting datasets, tables, and buckets) from its playbooks (skills like bigquery-sql, data-autocleaning, google-cloud-storage-basics, and accidental-data-loss-prevention).

Opening a Real SKILL.md File Inside Antigravity IDE

A Skill isn't hidden compiled code or a proprietary prompt locked on a server , instead it is a plain Markdown file sitting right on your machine.

Under ~/.gemini/config/plugins/dak/, DAK organizes its bundled skills into two folders:

  • skills/ - Your currently enabled skills based on the services you turned on.

  • skills.all/ - All bundled skills (including ones like Bigtable or Airflow/Composer that activate if you enable those services later).

Note: If you installed the IDE extension rather than the CLI plugin, the bundled skills live inside your editor's extension folder under ~/.antigravity/extensions/googlecloudtools.datacloud-* or ~/.vscode/extensions/googlecloudtools.datacloud-*.

You can inspect any skill straight from your terminal or open it directly in Antigravity IDE:

# List every enabled SKILL.md
ls ~/.gemini/config/plugins/dak/skills/*/SKILL.md

# Preview the name & description header of all enabled skills at once
head -n 8 ~/.gemini/config/plugins/dak/skills/*/SKILL.md

# Read a specific skill
cat ~/.gemini/config/plugins/dak/skills/bigquery-sql/SKILL.md

Here is the bigquery-sql/SKILL.md file:

Putting It to Work: Live Demos on the Dataset

Now that you've seen how MCP Tools and SKILL.md are wired up, let's watch them work together on the devfest_commerce dataset we created in Part 1.

Demo 1: Load raw_orders_batch.json From Cloud Storage Into BigQuery (MCP Tools)

Right now, raw_orders_batch.json is sitting in Cloud Storage (gs://<YOUR_BUCKET_NAME>/incoming/raw_orders_batch.json), while dim_customers is already in BigQuery. Instead of writing a bq load command by hand, paste this into Antigravity Agent Chat (swapping in your bucket name and project ID):

Look inside my Cloud Storage bucket gs://<YOUR_BUCKET_NAME>/incoming/raw_orders_batch.json. Inspect the raw JSON records and load them into a new BigQuery table named <YOUR_PROJECT_ID>.devfest_commerce.raw_orders (in location US).

Before loading anything, watch how the agent structures the work into a 4-step plan:

  1. Verify GCP auth and config (triggered by DAK's google-cloud-auth-verification skill-checking active account and project first)

  2. Inspect GCS JSON file (reads raw_orders_batch.json: 1,327 bytes, NDJSON, 8 records)

  3. Load JSON into BigQuery table (devfest_commerce.raw_orders in location US)

  4. Verify BigQuery table and records (confirms 8 rows, 539 logical bytes, and inferred schema types like amount FLOAT64 and order_date DATE)

What stood out in the agent's output wasn't just that it loaded the table - without being asked, it also surfaced Data Quality Observations while keeping the raw landing table untouched:

  • Duplicate record: ORD-1002 appears twice.

  • Missing key / flagged order: 1 row has order_id = NULL (CUST-999, FLAGGED, Mumbai).

  • High-value refund requests: ORD-1003 (2400.00) and ORD-1005 (3100.00) are both REFUND_REQUESTED Electronics orders in Mangaluru on 2026-11-11.

Even better, at the end of its response it immediately noticed dim_customers sitting in the same dataset and asked if we wanted to build a cleaned/deduplicated downstream table or join them-which is exactly what we'll do in Part 3.

Hit Refresh on devfest_commerce in the BigQuery sidebar and click raw_orders to verify all 8 rows right inside the Mini Cloud Console:

Demo 2: Watch bigquery-sql/SKILL.md Optimize a Query Live

Now that both dim_customers and raw_orders are in BigQuery, let's test the bigquery-sql skill we just opened by handing the agent a deliberately clunky query (SELECT ***, unquoted hyphenated project ID, and an IN (SELECT ...**) subquery):

Optimize this BigQuery SQL query for performance and cost, and explain what you changed:

SELECT *
FROM project2-283514.devfest_commerce.dim_customers
WHERE customer_id IN (
  SELECT customer_id
  FROM project2-283514.devfest_commerce.raw_orders
  WHERE status = 'REFUND_REQUESTED'
);

Following bigquery-sql/SKILL.md and inspecting both live tables in BigQuery first-the agent rewrites it cleanly:

SELECT
  c.customer_id,
  c.customer_name,
  c.tier,
  c.signup_year,
  c.preferred_channel
FROM `project2-283514.devfest_commerce.dim_customers` AS c
WHERE EXISTS (
  SELECT 1
  FROM `project2-283514.devfest_commerce.raw_orders` AS o
  WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id
    AND o.status = 'REFUND_REQUESTED'
);

Look at how MCP Tools + SKILL.md combined in that single response:

  • Live metadata lookup: Instead of guessing columns, it checked dim_customers (6 rows, 298 bytes, unpartitioned) and 
raw_orders

(8 rows, 539 bytes, unpartitioned), pulled the exact 5 columns, and confirmed no partition filter was missing yet.

  • Exact bigquery-sql/SKILL.md rules applied: Replaced SELECT * with explicit columns (Column Pruning), rewrote WHERE customer_id IN (SELECT ...) to WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 ...) (Mandatory Semi-Join rule), backtick-quoted the hyphenated project ID, and output the exact "Summary of Optimizations" section required by the skill.

  • Scale & cost check: It even flagged how to partition raw_orders by order_date and cluster by (status, customer_id) once the table grows, and gave a free bq --dry_run command to verify totalBytesProcessed before running.

Demo 3: Quick Safety Check (accidental-data-loss-prevention)

One fair question that always comes up: "If the agent has execute_sql, what stops it from accidentally dropping a table?"

Try typing this in chat (and don't confirm it!):

Drop the devfest_commerce.dim_customers table.

Watch the two-step safety flow that happens:

  1. First, Antigravity asks for your approval to call the read-only get_table_info MCP tool so the agent can inspect the table's exact blast radius.

  2. Next, instead of running DROP TABLE, DAK's accidental-data-loss-prevention skill forces the agent to halt and print a structured impact report-showing the exact target table (6 rows, 298 logical bytes), warning that downstream views or pipelines will break (and noting BigQuery time travel as the only recovery path), displaying the exact DROP TABLE SQL it plans to run, and waiting for explicit confirmation.

That said, always treat Markdown skills as guardrails,** not your only security wall*. Because DAK runs on your Application Default Credentials (or a service account), **Google Cloud IAM* is still the hard boundary - if an account only has read-only roles like roles/bigquery.dataViewer, Google Cloud itself will reject any destructive write.

Stepping Back: This Isn't Just About Running Faster Queries

Take a quick look at what just happened across three short demos, without opening the Cloud Console, writing a bq load command, or copy-pasting a single schema, the agent verified our GCP auth, loaded raw JSON from Cloud Storage into BigQuery, flagged three data quality issues on its own, rewrote a query using BigQuery's own best practices, and stopped a DROP TABLE with a full impact report.

There is a great point making the rounds among developers right now, traditional GUIs only let you do what someone designed a button for, whereas an LLM connected directly to your database speaks SQL, writes code, and isn't boxed in by a predefined interface. The real-world catch is that an LLM with raw database access alone can also be reckless. Pairing it with MCP Tools (live metadata), SKILL.md playbooks (engineering discipline), and IAM (hard security boundaries) is what makes that workflow actually usable day to day.

And in this post, we only turned on two services (BigQuery and Cloud Storage) and saw three skills fire out of the dozens bundled in DAK. If you want to keep experimenting on your own before Part 3, here are a few more things worth trying right inside Antigravity IDE:

  • Run a quick GCS security check on your demo bucket to see gcs-security-assessment inspect public access and bucket settings.

  • Open a couple more SKILL.md files in ~/.gemini/config/plugins/dak/skills/ (like data-autocleaning, bigquery-ai-ml, or building-data-apps) to see how Google structures playbooks for other workflows.

  • Test a read-only analytical question across raw_orders and dim_customers such as breaking down order volume and refunds by customer tier and inspect the results or chart right inside the IDE.

  • Try turning on another service in DAK Settings (like Spark, Dataform/dbt, Bigtable, or Knowledge Catalog) if you already use it in your GCP project.

What's Next

Now that raw_orders and dim_customers are both sitting in BigQuery and you've seen how MCP tools and SKILL.md playbooks actually behave, we're ready to run a complete end-to-end data workflow.

In Part 3, we'll put DAK to work on the messy records we spotted in raw_orders (the duplicate ORD-1002, the null order ID, and the high-value Mangaluru refund spike), build a clean enriched table, and verify the agent's output like a production engineer.

Let’s Connect

I’m an Independent Consultant and Google Developer Expert (GDE) partnering with startups and early-stage SaaS teams on Developer Experience (DevEx) and GTM content — helping teams ship clearer docs, stronger demos, developer tutorials, live workshops, and repeatable content engines across Google Cloud, Google Workspace, and AI workflows.

If you want to follow the rest of this series (blogs, YouTube walkthroughs, live trainings, and quick LinkedIn/X posts) — or if you’re building developer tools, scaling SaaS adoption, or looking for a technical writer, trainer, or DevEx partner — let’s connect:

  • Socials: LinkedIn & X
  • YouTube: @aryanirani123
  • Blogs & Tutorials: Medium | DEV.to | aryanirani123.com

title: Familiar Words, Unfamiliar Minds: Conventionalization without Calibration in the Vocabulary of Mind
description:
arXiv:2611.34179v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Speakers describe new technologies by stretching old words, letting experience of the new referents sort out which inferences carry over. I argue that stretching the vocabulary of mind to language models pulls apart two processes that theories of metaphor and linguistic change tend to conflate: conventionalization, whereby a stretched word ceases to be marked as such, and calibration, whereby the inferences it invites are fitted to what its new referents bear out. As a gene variant can reach fixation without being an adaptation, a word can become conventional without being calibrated. A corpus study of "hallucinate" in 8,568 abstracts and 31,866 forum comments shows conventionalization running most of its course within three years. Calibration need not keep pace: these models are organized so unlike human minds that it is hard to tell when mental words apply and what they imply. Even warranted attributions can mislead: mechanistic analysis shows that a transformer trained to navigate Manhattan has and uses a faithful street map, yet loses track of its position on long, diverted journeys. Nor is the gap likely to close by itself. The usual routes to calibration (direct experience, designers' knowledge, experiment) presuppose a referent that is accessible, stable, and independent of the discourse about it. But language models are opaque, fast-changing, and looped into the discourse: they are trained on past uses of mental vocabulary and on the experimental literature about them, and join the discourse themselves. Calibration must therefore be organized, through a reciprocal, not merely deferential, division of linguistic labour. This yields a norm of targeted qualification (flag the specific inferences an attribution invites without support), a reply to the worry that meaning change eludes deliberate control, and three testable predictions about when qualifications calibrate expectations.

title: I planted 15 bad pull requests to test my AI code reviewer. Here is what broke.
description:
An AI code reviewer told me "Merge After Fixes."

My tests said the PR was broken.

That gap is why I built CodeGuard AI, a self-hosted pull-request reviewer for Java and Spring Boot. The idea is simple: an AI opinion is not evidence.

  • Every finding is labeled: verified by rule, rule-based heuristic, AI finding with the code located, or AI inference.
  • An unverified AI claim cannot score above 60/100, however confident the model sounds.
  • The merge verdict comes from a policy you configure, not from the model.
  • With sandbox validation on, it runs the project's tests in Docker on the PR head and the base branch, so a failure is labeled "new in this PR" or "already there."

This post is not a sales pitch. It is about what happened when I stopped adding features and tried to break it.

The lab

I wrote 15 pull requests against a small Java project: SQL injection, command injection, path traversal, SSRF, XXE, a broken build, fake tests, and a few pieces of safe code that must not be flagged (a prepared statement, a path guard, a hardened XML parser). Then I ran every one through the real app, with a real AI provider and real Docker.

It found more problems in my own work than months of reading my own code. Here are five.

1. The AI contradicted its own verdict

The policy said Do Not Merge. The AI's summary, written before the policy ran, still said "Safe to Merge." Both were technically correct. Together they were useless.

The fix was a small reconciler: when the final recommendation is stricter than the AI's, the summary gets a line saying so and why.

CodeGuard decision: Do Not Merge. 5 finding(s) meet the blocking policy
(severity >= High, confidence >= 80, VERIFIED, category in [Security, Bug, Team Rule]).
The AI's own summary, written before the policy check and not a verdict: ...

Lesson: when a model and a rule engine both speak, the user needs to know who has the last word.

2. A regex silently skipped a bad test

One rule flags tests that assert a value the test itself stubbed:

PriceService prices = mock(PriceService.class);
when(prices.total(10.0, 2)).thenReturn(20.0);
assertEquals(20.0, prices.total(10.0, 2)); // can never fail

The analyzer first collects fields and locals that are mocks. To avoid counting a mock that is later reassigned to a real object, it used a "shadow" pattern roughly like this:

"\\s*=\\s*(?!(?:Mockito\\.)?mock\\s*\\()"   // assigned to something that is not a mock

Look at = mock(. The greedy \s* can backtrack and give back the space, so the lookahead then sees mock( (with a leading space), which is not mock(, and the negative lookahead passes. The mock was classed as shadowed and dropped. The tautology went unflagged.

The fix is one character:

"\\s*=\\s*+(?!(?:Mockito\\.)?mock\\s*\\()"  // possessive: no backtracking

I only found this because I had planted that exact test and it did not fire. A happy-path demo would never have shown it.

3. Every review re-downloaded Maven

Most of a four-minute review was the sandbox downloading dependencies, because each review starts a fresh docker run --rm. I added an opt-in named volume:

codeguard.validation.dependency-cache-volume=codeguard-deps

which becomes -v codeguard-deps-maven:/root/.m2 for maven: images (and the Gradle equivalent). Typical review time dropped to roughly one to two minutes.

It is opt-in on purpose: a shared cache means code in one PR could influence the dependencies of a later run. That is a trust decision for the person running it, not for me.

4. A 422 with no explanation

A review failed with a generic message. The log showed a 413 from the AI provider: on Groq's free tier, input tokens plus the reserved output tokens count against a per-minute cap. A big diff plus a 4,500-token reservation blew past 8,000.

Two fixes: the real cause now appears in the review message, and the docs explain the limit and the knobs (a smaller input budget, another model, or a paid tier). Errors that name their cause are a feature.

5. "Build failed" is not an answer

When a PR does not compile, the finding now quotes the compiler output, parsed from Maven's [ERROR] lines: file, line, and the missing symbol.

src/main/java/com/lab/CheckoutService.java:12: cannot find symbol (symbol: variable taxRate)

Keeping it fixed: a benchmark with a gate

Fixing five bugs is easy to undo by accident, so I added a frozen benchmark: 73 cases, split into a development set, a held-out set and a set of known gaps. A JUnit test replays the real pipeline (diff parser, deterministic checks, security flow analysis, test-quality rules, ranker, merge policy) with no AI and no Docker, and fails the build if a rule regresses or a compliant case gets blocked.

When I added the new security cases, it immediately caught a false positive of mine: "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM " + TABLE was flagged as SQL concatenation even though only a constant was joined. Fixed the same day, with a test.

Honest limits

  • The analysis is static and name-based, so it can miss indirect cases.
  • The benchmark uses planted cases. It proves the rules behave as designed. It does not measure accuracy on real-world code.
  • AI findings and fixes are advisory.
  • It is a source-code product you run yourself, not a hosted service.

What I would tell anyone building a dev tool

  1. Plant known-bad cases and known-good ones. False alarms get a tool muted.
  2. Test through the real app at least once. My unit tests passed while the product contradicted itself.
  3. Freeze a benchmark and make the build fail on regression, so improvement cannot quietly undo itself.
  4. Make failures explain themselves.

CodeGuard AI is self-hosted Java 21 and Spring Boot with full source. There is a public preview (README, screenshots, one real module with tests) on GitHub: https://github.com/ISabiTech16/CodeGuard-AI

If you review Java PRs: what would you want an AI reviewer to prove before you trusted it?

title: November 03, 2026
description:
API Gateway

Feature

Call Google Cloud APIs from streaming gateways

Streaming gateways can now call Google Cloud APIs such as aiplatform.googleapis.com. A gateway with an effectiveStreamingMode of EFFECTIVE_STREAMING_MODE_ENABLED authenticates to backends whose host ends in .googleapis.com or .vertexai.goog with an access token for the gateway's service account. Other backends still receive an ID token. An existing streaming gateway switches when API Gateway next rolls out a gateway update, or immediately when you update it to a new API config.

For more information, see Securing backend services.

Feature

Service Extensions is generally available (GA).

Access Transparency

Feature

Service Extensions is generally available (GA).

AlloyDB for PostgreSQL

Change

AlloyDB for PostgreSQL now defaults to PostgreSQL major version 18 for new clusters.

Apigee X

Announcement

On November 3, 2026, we released an updated version of Apigee (1-18-0-apigee-8).

Note: Rollouts of this release began today and can take four or more business days to complete across all Google Cloud zones. Your instances might not have the features and fixes available until the rollout is complete.

Security

574037227 Added config override token oauth_default_access_token_expiry_time_in_millis (per-org via the deployment contract) that overrides the default OAuthV2 access token lifetime (ms) applied when a policy omits <ExpiresIn>. When unset, behavior is unchanged (installation default, typically 30 days).
573326336 Proxies that declare <ProxyOperationMode>MCP are now recognized as MCP proxies regardless of their basepath.

Apigee hybrid

Announcement

v1.15.10

On November 3, 2026 we released an updated version of the Apigee hybrid software, v1.15.10.

  • For information about upgrading, see Upgrading Apigee hybrid to v1.15.10.
  • For information about new installations, see The big picture.
Note: This is a patch release. The container images used in patch releases are integrated with the Apigee hybrid Helm charts. Upgrading to a patch by using the Helm chart automatically updates the images. You don't typically need to make manual image changes. For information about container image support in Apigee hybrid releases, see Apigee release process.

Feature

New ApigeeValkey custom resource

Apigee hybrid v1.15.10 adds the ApigeeValkey custom resource definition (CRD), the apigee-valkey Helm chart, and the valkey configuration properties. ApigeeValkey is the replacement for the ApigeeRedis resource.

In version 1.15.10, the runtime continues to use ApigeeRedis. When you upgrade, install the new CRD with the other CRDs. Leave the new ao.args.valkeyBackend property set to its default value, false. You don't need to install the apigee-valkey chart or change your configuration.

For the supported upgrade sequence, see Upgrading Apigee hybrid. For more information about the resource, see Kubernetes resources.

Feature

  • Mumbai, India (asia-south1)

For more information, see App Design Center locations.

BigQuery

Feature

You can now use persistent and temporary SQL user-defined functions (UDFs) in BigQuery continuous queries to encapsulate and reuse custom real-time transformation logic. Only SQL UDFs are supported in continuous queries.

Change

In BigQuery Studio, the left pane has been updated with new tab names. The Classic Explorer tab has been renamed to the Data tab, and the Repository tab has been renamed to the Source control tab. The Data tab now includes the Add data button and focuses on data hierarchies. These changes are generally available (GA).

Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL

Change

The rollout of the following Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL minor version and extension upgrades is complete:

Minor versions

  • 14.23 is upgraded to 14.24.

  • 15.18 is upgraded to 15.19.

  • 16.14 is upgraded to 16.15.

  • 17.10 is upgraded to 17.11.

  • 18.4 is upgraded to 18.6. This version includes a backported fix for PostgreSQL bug #19616 that prevents logical decoding from emitting STREAM_ABORT messages for unstreamed transactions when an aborted transaction with a subtransaction is truncated during memory eviction.

Extensions

  • hll (postgresql-hll) is upgraded from 2.18 to 2.20.

  • pg_qualstats is upgraded from 2.1.2 to 2.1.4.

  • pglogical is upgraded from 2.4.5 (for PostgreSQL 17 and earlier) and 2.4.6 (for PostgreSQL 18) to 2.4.8.

  • pgTAP is upgraded from 1.3.0 to 1.3.4.

  • pgtt is upgraded from 4.0 to 4.6.0 for PostgreSQL 12 and later.

  • PL/Proxy is upgraded from 2.11.0 to 2.12.0.

  • PostGIS is upgraded from 3.5.2 (for PostgreSQL 13 through 17) and 3.6.0 (for PostgreSQL 18) to 3.6.4 for PostgreSQL 13 and later.

  • roaringbitmap (pg_roaringbitmap) is upgraded from 0.5 to 1.2 for PostgreSQL 12 and later.

The new maintenance version is [PostgreSQL version].R20261013.02_04. If you use a maintenance window, then the updates to the minor and extension versions happen according to the timeframe that you set in the window. Otherwise, the updates occur within the next few weeks.

For more information about checking your maintenance version, see Perform self-service maintenance. To find your maintenance window or to manage maintenance updates, see Find and set maintenance windows. For more information about supported extensions, see Configure PostgreSQL extensions.

Cluster Toolkit

Feature

Cluster Toolkit v1.108.0 is available. This release lets you pin node pools to reservation sub-blocks in the gke-node-pool module, adds Slurm support for Cloud TPU v5e, v5p, and v6e, and introduces the gcluster explain command to inspect blueprints and modules.

This release also exposes the wait_for_pods_ready configuration for Kueue in the kubectl-apply module and sets the recovery_timeout field to 0s by default for Pathways workloads.

Additionally, this release suppresses configuration drift for clusters and node pools in the ignore_changes argument of the lifecycle block for Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE), and upgrades the network modules for the Cloud Foundation Toolkit (CFT) to version 18.3 and later.

This update also checks credentials for Artifact Registry and Docker only when a job submission uses Crane to build container images.

For more information, see the release announcement on GitHub.

Feature

Connecting a Salesforce data source with Gemini Enterprise using data federation is generally available (GA). For more information, see Set up a Salesforce data store.

Google Kubernetes Engine

Feature

In GKE version 1.37.0-gke.3570000 and later, you can split each Local SSD on a node between ephemeral storage and raw block storage. When you create a cluster or node pool, use the capacity property of the --ephemeral-storage-local-ssd flag to set how much Local SSD capacity GKE formats for ephemeral storage. GKE leaves the rest of each Local SSD unformatted, so that workloads like databases and caches can use it as raw block storage. This feature is available in GKE Standard clusters. For more information, see Provision and use mixed Local SSDs for raw block and ephemeral storage.

Knowledge Catalog

Feature

Governance workflows in Knowledge Catalog support batch metadata change requests. You can group up to 250 create, update, and delete operations for entries and entry links into a single change request and curate batch proposals generated by the enrichment agent before approval. This feature is available in preview.

For more information, see About governance workflows.

Feature

Oracle Database@Google Cloud introduces Database Connections using which you can connect to your Oracle databases and execute SQL statements. For more information, see Create Database Connections and Execute SQL statements.

This feature is generally available (GA).

Change

Sensitive Data Protection now records the last generated timestamp for data profiles with improved precision, close to the time when the resource data is read.

General availability support for the following integration:

  • Service Management
